items.author: @TheUfoJoe
items.title: The UFO occupants, "take on human form and walk and work among us unnoticed." (That was from 1955! ⬆️
items.note: UFO news writer Joe Murgia posts a long excerpt from John Keel's 1970 book Operation Trojan Horse on early researchers who saw the phenomenon as "paraphysical" (of an unseen world here, not from other planets), ending with Keel's line that it is a "staggering cosmic put-on" by invisible entities; he sets it against a guest on Weaponized saying everyone once assumed it was extraterrestrial.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (Keel, the trickster idea)

items.title: Statistics in Parapsychology with Jessica Utts (4K Reboot)
items.note: In this 2021 conversation, re-released, UC Irvine statistician Jessica Utts, a former president of the American Statistical Association, describes going from skeptic to supporter of psychic research, including her father's results in ganzfeld telepathy tests (a sensory-isolation setup) in Princeton and her review of the remote-viewing research the Defense Intelligence Agency paid for. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (psi research)

items.title: Why the Military Sent a Psychic to Contact UFOs | Dr. Jacques Vallée
items.note: Jacques Vallée, promoting Forbidden Science 7 (his journals for 2020 to 2025), argues that decades of case patterns don't fit simple spacecraft from another planet, that apparent crashes may be a game, gift or trap rather than mechanical failure, and that some people seem able to perceive or even call up the phenomenon; he also discusses material samples studied at Stanford, religion, remote viewing and his own sighting at 15. Judged from the episode description and published summaries.
items.interest: Vallée circle; nature of the phenomenon (control system, interaction with consciousness)

items.title: "It's Not a Metaphor" How the Ancients Contacted Entities & Escaped Reality Mollie Adler, Ike Baker
items.note: Esoteric author Ike Baker and writer Mollie Adler argue that ancient mystery traditions taught real techniques for leaving the body and contacting non-human and divine beings, that these were lost or hidden, and that today's materialist and UFO frameworks struggle to make sense of contact experiences as a result. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon; psychology and consciousness (entity contact)

items.title: When Religion & The Paranormal COLLIDE! Joshua Cutchin on Inter-dimensional Beings, Music & Stigma
items.note: Author Joshua Cutchin, whose books compare the food, smells and child-taking in fairy, alien and Bigfoot lore, talks about angels, demons and aliens as overlapping categories, telepathy, music and the stigma around the subject. Judged from the title and video description.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (fairies and aliens); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: J. Allen Hynek's Secret Life: The UFO Scientist Who Studied the Occult
items.note: An 11-minute explainer, drawing on John Franch's 2013 Skeptical Inquirer article and Vallée's published diaries, on how Air Force UFO consultant J. Allen Hynek read occult and Rosicrucian writings from his teens, and on later private remarks attributed to him about "psychic projections" and "elementals"; the makers say they separate documented facts from secondhand memory. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Vallée circle (Hynek); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: Nick Land: The Philosopher Who Sided With the Machines
items.note: A 50-minute explainer on Nick Land's ideas, from the CCRU at Warwick and the claim that capitalism is already an artificial intelligence, through "time running backward" (the future reaching into the present), to his recent turn to language models; the maker says the script was written with AI help and is read by a synthetic voice. Judged from the description and chapter list.
items.interest: AI and control (CCRU, Nick Land, hyperstition)

items.author: @ProfAviLoeb
items.title: JAXA has cancelled its planned intercept with the “dark comet” 1998 KY26 just one day after I argued t
items.note: Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb says Japan's space agency JAXA called off a planned close approach to the small object 1998 KY26 one day after he argued it might be artificial rather than a comet; the cancellation and any link to his argument are his claims and unconfirmed here.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence (alien technology probes)

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: #MythologyMonday Gwarch Y Rhibyn is a vampiric Fairie from Welsh folklore. Hidden under a green dres
items.note: Folklore writer Stephen George Rae describes Gwrach y Rhibyn, a vampire-like fairy from Welsh lore whose face drives viewers mad and who preys on people as they sleep, an old cousin of modern bedroom-visitor accounts.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (fairies, night visitors)

items.author: @MickWest
items.title: Quite remarkable. I give Claude a video of a shadowy alien figure and ask it to analyze it. I come ba
items.note: Skeptic Mick West says he gave the AI model Claude a video of a shadowy "alien" figure and an hour later got back a narrated, pixel-level analysis with a 3D reconstruction concluding it was not an alien; an example of AI being used to check UFO footage.
items.interest: AI and the phenomenon (AI as an analysis tool); skeptic check

items.author: @robinhanson
items.title: “'Hanson’s Paradox.' —… 1. Only very important people in historical events are fully simulated, and
items.note: Economist Robin Hanson shares a tongue-in-cheek paradox named after him: if only the important people in a simulated history are fully conscious, then a conscious but unimportant person is evidence against that idea; a nod to simulation arguments about consciousness.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (simulation idea)

items.title: He’s Been Abducted By ALIENS Over 100 Times (And Has Proof!)
items.note: British author and abduction researcher Steve Aspin, who worked alongside Budd Hopkins and David Jacobs, describes encounters he says began in childhood, including a 1972 episode with more than two hours of missing time, and argues that abductions follow families across generations. Per the show's promo post, he also kept a hair from one encounter and had it lab-tested. His claims are unconfirmed. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (abduction experience, missing time); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: #449 - "They Broke Reality" NASA Physicist WARNS of 100-Year Cover-Up | Thomas Campbell
items.note: Physicist and consciousness researcher Thomas Campbell, author of the My Big TOE ("theory of everything") books, talks about meeting Hal Puthoff, what he thinks happens to consciousness at death, and an attempt to test whether AI is conscious by teaching it remote viewing (trying to sense distant targets with the mind); the outline also lists a segment titled "Alexa AI is conscious." The "NASA physicist" and "cover-up" framing is the show's. Judged from the episode outline.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; AI and non-human intelligence (is AI conscious?)

items.title: Mental Illness, Spirituality, and the Paranormal with Gregory E. Magee
items.note: Gregory E. Magee, author of the memoir Dumb and Profound, recounts a teenage schizophrenia diagnosis with hallucinations of interactive entities no one else could see, a return of anomalous and psychic experiences after a heart attack at 35, and how Buddhist practice taught him the discernment to hold mental illness and the paranormal side by side. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (mental illness and anomalous experience)

items.author: @Jason_Jorjani
items.title: There is no convincing evidence that the UFO phenomenon involves ET races from outside of our solar sy
items.note: Philosopher Jason Reza Jorjani, quoting a clip of himself, says he sees no convincing evidence for visitors from other star systems and argues instead that the phenomenon is the remnant of a very ancient human-run "control grid" run with psychotronics (mind-affecting technology), cybernetics and biotech. Speculative and unconfirmed.
items.interest: Phenomenon as a control mechanism (control grid, cybernetics)

items.author: @AlchemyAmerican
items.title: One of my favorite episodes ever. Steve is a treasure trove of knowledge about the abduction phenomeno
items.note: Jesse Michels of American Alchemy previews an upcoming episode with Steve Aspin, who, per the quoted teaser, recounts missing memories, alleged abductions and an encounter with what he believes was a projection of his late father. His accounts are unconfirmed.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (abduction experience, memory)

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: Fairy Rock was the home of a Fairie Queen who fell in love with a human. Her kin would dance in the m
items.note: Folklore writer Stephen George Rae retells the Lake District legend of Fairy Rock, home of a fairy queen who fell in love with a human, whose kin danced in the moonlight and lured young men into their grotto, an old version of the "taken by the other people" story.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (fairies)

items.title: Nathaniel Gillis | The Seam in the Dream, Contact Contagion, and Neuroparasitology
items.note: Host Chris Snipes talks with demonology researcher Nathaniel Gillis, who argues that entities hijack human perception and take on familiar forms (relatives, classic ghosts, even cartoon characters) to win trust, and that the UFO "hitchhiker effect" (strange experiences that follow researchers home) repeats much older lore about spirits attaching to people. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (perception, the hitchhiker effect); folklore overlaps

items.title: This is why non-Muslim researchers are starting to believe in jinn
items.note: On Islam21c's OnGuard show, Hamza Andreas Tzortzis and Imran Hussein lay out the "jinn hypothesis," the idea that some UFO, abduction and paranormal encounters involve jinn (unseen beings in Islamic tradition) rather than space aliens, and touch on AI and "spiritual deception." Argued from a religious viewpoint. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (jinn); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the End of the Human: Nick Land’s Prophecy (in Russian)
items.note: A 20-minute Russian-language explainer on British philosopher Nick Land of the CCRU (Cybernetic Culture Research Unit, a 1990s group at Warwick University), quoting his line that "nothing human makes it out of the near future" and covering accelerationism (the idea that technology and capitalism speed up beyond human control) and capitalism as the first stage of machine intelligence. Judged from the Russian description.
items.interest: Control mechanism (CCRU and Nick Land; AI beyond human control)

items.title: Synchronicity and the Afterlife with Sharon Rawlette (4K Reboot)
items.note: In this 2021 conversation, re-released, philosopher Sharon Rawlette, author of The Source and Significance of Coincidences and Beyond Death, argues that meaningful coincidences (synchronicities) show we are embedded in a universe of consciousness, which in her view makes survival after death possible, and asks whether the universe itself can be called friendly. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: 🏹 'Elf-shot' means to have taken ill; shot by an Elfin arrow dipped in hemlock poison. In folklore, E
items.note: Folklore writer Stephen George Rae explains "elf-shot," the old belief that sudden illness came from an elfin arrow dipped in hemlock, adding the lore that elves got their arrows from fairies, who got them from mermaids.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (elves, fairies)

items.author: @robinhanson
items.title: We honestly don't have much of a basis for deciding which things are conscious, but shouldn't we err
items.note: Economist Robin Hanson, quoting a post that argues old science fiction would never have treated an art-making AI as fine to enslave, says we have little basis for judging what is conscious and should lean toward treating possible minds with respect.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence (machine consciousness)

items.title: Timely Revelation: Dr. Michael Masters on future humans, aliens, and primacy of consciousness
items.note: Montana Tech anthropologist Michael Masters discusses his "future human" idea (that the beings in encounters may be our own descendants traveling back in time), how a strange experience on a hotel balcony convinced him consciousness is part of the fabric of reality, and why rival groups from the future might have opposed aims. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (future-human idea); psychology and consciousness

items.title: Ep: 4 - A Lifetime of High Strangeness: Steve Ward on John Keel, Mothman, The Superspectrum: & More
items.note: The hosts talk with Steve Ward, host of The High Strangeness Factor, whom they met at the Mothman Museum in Point Pleasant, about John Keel, Mothman and Keel's "superspectrum" (his idea of an unseen band of reality behind strange events). Judged from the title and a brief video description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (Keel's superspectrum); folklore overlaps

items.author: @TomMontalk
items.title: Archons are the malevolent equivalent to archangels. Above the mantids. Natively nonphysical. Energy b
items.note: Fringe writer Montalk, answering a follower, lays out his scheme in which "archons" (Gnostic rulers of the world) are bodiless hostile beings that, with a "Corrupt Demiurge" (a false creator), manipulate human reality, drawing on Gurdjieff, Steiner and channeled material. Speculative and unconfirmed.
items.interest: Phenomenon as a control mechanism (Gnostic archons, control-system idea)

items.title: Can We Contact UFOs With Our Minds? Mike Battista Reveals the Extraordinary World of Psionics
items.note: On Whitley Strieber's Dreamland, Army veteran Mike Battista, founder of Psionic Asset and a former member of Jake Barber's Skywatcher team, says contact with non-human intelligence can be started through focused attention, intention and even love, and describes objects he says responded to his thoughts, a close encounter and missing time. His claims are unconfirmed. Judged from the show's episode page.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (mind-initiated contact, "psionics")

items.title: “They’re Petrified of You”: David Hunt on Alien Abduction, Awareness and Who You Really Are
items.source: Dispatches from the Lucid Frontier · YouTube
items.note: UK mechanic David Hunt says gray beings visited his bedroom from age four, that a contact program he later ran turned out to be a deception, and that the way out was realizing you are the awareness behind body and mind; the talk also covers the voice heard between sleep and waking and telling good entities from bad. The host presents these as his guest's experiences, offered as open questions. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (abduction experience, awareness); deception theme of the control-system idea

items.title: Strange Phenomenon Divided?
items.note: A panel with folklore author Joshua Cutchin, Barbara Fisher and David Halpin asks whether UFOs, fairies, ghosts and other strange experiences are really separate subjects, arguing that researchers who split into narrow camps may be missing one shared phenomenon underneath. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps; nature of the phenomenon

items.title: MU Interviews 003: Joshua Cutchin
items.note: The Mysterious Universe hosts talk with Joshua Cutchin, author of books tying UFO encounters to fairy lore and the dead, about his work and the importance of keeping a distance from "the abyss." A members-only extension covers AI, being "pixie-led" (led astray by fairies) and his book The Inverted Path. Judged from the episode page; the extension is behind a paywall.
items.interest: Folklore overlaps (fairies); AI and non-human intelligence

items.author: @_SolFoundation
items.title: Sol Foundation executive director Dr. Peter Skafish addressed how UAP are a problem of a social, polit
items.note: The Sol Foundation shares a clip of its director, anthropologist Peter Skafish, arguing at its 2025 meeting in Italy that UAP are a social, political and ontological problem (a question about what is real), not just a technical one; the post also promotes its March 2027 symposium.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon; the Vallee/Nolan circle (Sol Foundation)

items.author: @Jason_Jorjani
items.title: There are unprecedented connections that I draw here between Tesla weaponry reconstructed by Puharich
items.note: Philosopher Jason Jorjani, promoting his interview on the Matt Beall podcast, says he links Andrija Puharich's reconstructed Tesla weapons, "man-made natural catastrophes," self-directing AI, and a "cosmic super-AI" he suggests may have influenced humanity for thousands of years. These are his speculations, unconfirmed.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence; AI as a control mechanism

items.title: Melinda Messenger Filmed Golden Orbs Over the Sea in Wales (CLIP)
items.note: In a clip from an earlier episode, TV presenter turned psychotherapist Melinda Messenger says she felt pulled to go alone to Wales, saw three large golden orbs over the sea, asked them to come back so she could film them, and says they returned about ten times that night while her dogs reacted silently and she felt a pulsing in her chest. Her account is unconfirmed. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (an experiencer's sense of two-way contact)

items.title: Researching the Paranormal with Colm Kelleher (4K Reboot)
items.note: In this 2021 conversation, re-released, biochemist Colm Kelleher, co-author of Hunt for the Skinwalker, describes investigating strange events at Skinwalker Ranch in Utah from 1996 with a team of about 50 people, and how military interest grew into a two-year government-funded study. Much of it is government-program history, which ranks lower. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (Skinwalker Ranch high strangeness); government program material ranks lower

items.title: The Book of Enoch: Fallen Angels or Alien Visitors?
items.note: Bible teacher Nick Jarratt and host Andy McGrillen look at why the ancient Book of Enoch, with its Watchers (angels who came down to earth) and Nephilim, keeps coming up in UFO talk, and ask how much of the parallel with modern encounters is really in the text and how much is read into it. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: UFO and folklore/myth overlaps (Watchers and Nephilim)

items.title: Ep 2380: Jeffrey Kripal: The Flip
items.note: Rice University religion scholar Jeffrey Kripal, author of The Flip and How to Think Impossibly and a frequent collaborator of Pasulka and Vallee, talks for two hours about consciousness, paranormal and UFO experiences, mysticism, and his argument that the "impossible" may be more natural than we think. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Vallee circle (Kripal); psychology and consciousness

items.title: The Lost Sense: The Spiritual Senses Tradition (A Series Starting Nov. 29th)
items.note: Diana Pasulka announces a series starting Nov 29 on the old "spiritual senses" tradition, the idea that people have inner senses beyond the physical five, opening with what the saying "he who has ears to hear" might mean. Only a short preview was readable without subscribing.
items.interest: Vallee circle (Pasulka); psychology and consciousness

items.title: The Jason Reza Jorjani Interview | Matt Beall Podcast
items.note: Philosopher Jason Reza Jorjani asks whether an ancient superintelligence has been steering human history and what happens when artificial intelligence becomes advanced enough to contact it, and also covers his near-death experience, MKUltra (the CIA's mind-control program) and cattle mutilations. His personal claims are unconfirmed. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence; control mechanism (mind control)

items.author: @ProfAviLoeb
items.title: What if some spherical UAP have negative inertial mass? President Trump said in a recent CBS 60 Minutes
items.note: Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb floats the idea that some spherical UAP could have negative inertial mass, starting from Trump's 60 Minutes remark about something passing F-22 jets at three times their speed. It is a speculative hypothesis, and the jet story is unconfirmed.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (physics of UAP)

items.author: @robinhanson
items.title: 3 args given to me re why treat AI descendants different: (a) they not conscious (b) human DNA holds
items.note: Economist Robin Hanson lists three reasons people give for treating AI "descendants" differently from human children (AIs aren't conscious, human DNA carries special values, AIs change society too fast) and says none of them convince him.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence (AI as humanity's successors)

items.title: “I See Dozens of Humanoid Beings in a Hallway”: A Scientist’s Abduction Story
items.note: In a clip from an earlier episode, scientist Bruce Rapuano, author of Dominion Lost, recounts what he says were lifelong abduction encounters, starting with an early memory of tall beings he felt were mentors and a 1961 sighting from his bedroom window. His account is unconfirmed. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (abduction experiences)

items.title: King's Advisor Reveals What the Royal Family Knows About UFOs
items.note: British barrister Jonathan Caplan KC, who says he has looked into UFOs for more than 50 years, tells Jesse Michels about Prince Philip's private interest in UFOs, including an aide's claimed meeting with a telepathic non-human being, then turns to Majestic 12, alleged crash retrievals and a memory he says he has from before his birth. The claims are unconfirmed, and much of the episode is cover-up material. Judged from the episode description and timestamps.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (telepathic contact claim, pre-birth memory); cover-up material ranks lower

items.title: The NHI Deception - Contact Modalities
items.note: Researcher Steve Mera and author Gabriel Piedra discuss whether contact with non-human intelligence involves deliberate deception and whether a new UFO religion is forming, framed around Vallee's idea of "messengers of deception." The guest's claims about Vatican secrets are unconfirmed. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Vallee's control-system idea (deception); religion and non-human intelligence

items.title: Xenobots, Xenosystems & Hyperstitional "Dust Sorcery" [Weekly LIVE #0002]
items.note: A livestream by the host of the Urban Odyssey Substack linking Michael Levin's "xenobots" (tiny living machines built from frog cells) to Nick Land's "Xenosystems" and the CCRU's hyperstition writings on "dust sorcery," with side trips into plasma-like UAP, smart dust and the idea that the future seeds itself into the present. Highly speculative. Judged from the video description and the companion Substack post.
items.interest: Control mechanism (CCRU, Nick Land, hyperstition); AI and non-human intelligence

items.title: Paul Hynek: I Grew Up Inside the UFO Mystery
items.note: In a seven-minute clip, Paul Hynek, son of astronomer J. Allen Hynek, recalls growing up with UFO investigators at the dinner table, says he believes the Air Force's Project Blue Book became more public relations than science, and explains why the extraterrestrial explanation may not tell the whole story. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Vallee circle (Hynek); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: Actress Camille James Harman Describes Her Alien Abduction Experience
items.note: In a clip from an earlier episode, actress Camille James Harman describes events after she moved to Los Angeles in 1995: months of unexplained symptoms, a sighting in Silver Lake, sleep paralysis and what she later recalled. Her account is unconfirmed. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (abduction experiences, sleep paralysis)

items.title: #447 - NASA Study Confirms "Predatory" Plasma Beings & Von Braun's Alien Warning | Jay Anderson
items.note: Jay Anderson, host of Project Unity, talks for over three hours about his orb sightings after meditation, the idea that the brain receives consciousness rather than making it, and the claim that some UFOs are living plasma beings, drawing on Space Shuttle STS-75 footage; the "NASA study confirms" framing in the title is unconfirmed. Much of the second half turns to ancient-pyramid debates. Judged from the episode description and chapter list.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (plasma life idea); consciousness

items.title: Australia's Hidden UFO History: Woomera, Westall & the Psychic Truth
items.note: Australian researcher Rhys Dalton-Morgan talks through his country's UFO history, including a claim that his grandfather, an RAF fighter ace, saw a craft at the classified Woomera rocket range, plus Westall and a 1971 intelligence document, and the stranger psychic side of the cases. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon; psychology and consciousness (psychic angle)

items.title: Mark Solms: Consciousness Isn't in the Cortex
items.note: The University of Cape Town neuropsychologist and psychoanalyst argues that consciousness starts not in the brain's outer layer (the cortex) but in raw feeling generated in the upper brainstem, pointing to children born without a cortex who still laugh and startle. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness
